title: Quasi-coherent cohomological dimension of algebraic-space curve families
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to T$ a proper, flat, finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] whose geometric fibres have dimension at most one (the empty fibre is allowed). Flatness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts, and proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed. For any $F\in\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], the higher direct image sheaves $R^qf_*F$, computed on the small etale sites by injective resolutions of module sheaves, vanish for $q>1$. For every affine base change $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$ and every quasi-coherent module $G$ on $X_V=X\times_TV$, including modules not pulled back from $X$, one has
$$H^q(X_V,G)=0\quad(q>1).$$
Here $H^q$ is the right derived functor of sections of module sheaves. The base scheme and the quasi-coherent modules need not be Noetherian or coherent, respectively. No nodal, reduced, connected or Gorenstein hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0E6F (lemma-etale-locally-scheme) reduces families of curves etale locally on the base to proper schemes; limits.tex Tag 0E7D (lemma-higher-direct-images-zero-above-dimension-fibre) gives vanishing for arbitrary quasi-coherent modules over arbitrary scheme bases. Descent of higher direct images uses flat etale base change; this is not an application of spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 0A4T without its locally Noetherian hypothesis.

proof.text: Choose an etale scheme covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ such that $X_i=X\times_TT_i$ is a scheme, using [lem-sfb-curve-etale-scheme-cover]. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] each $f_i:X_i\to T_i$ is proper, flat and finitely presented. The base-change invariance in [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-fibre-dimension], applied also to algebraic closures of residue fields, gives $\dim (X_i)_t\leq1$ for every $t\in T_i$, including empty fibres.

source.place: Tag 0E6F; spaces-morphisms.tex base-change lemmas and spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0D4N.

proof.text: Restrict $F$ to $X_i$. It is still quasi-coherent: restrict each local presentation in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] to the slice etale site, where the same covering and exact presentation apply. By [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-higher-image-comparison] it corresponds to a quasi-coherent Zariski module $F_i$ and $R^qf_{i,\mathrm{et},*}(F|_{X_i})\cong(R^qf_{i,\mathrm{Zar},*}F_i)_{\mathrm{et}}$. Properness makes $f_i$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-quasicoherent-fibre-dimension-vanishing] with $d=1$: the right side is zero for $q>1$.

For $q>1$, [lem-sfb-space-higher-image-etale-restriction] identifies $(R^qf_*F)|_{T_i}$ with the zero sheaf found in step 2. Hence $R^qf_*F=0$: for any etale object $U\to T$, the base-changed family $\{U\times_TT_i\to U\}$ covers $U$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; each restriction of a section is zero, so the sheaf equalizer condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes that section zero. This proves the relative assertion on all of $T$.

source.place: Tag 03LX; sheaf separatedness along a covering.

proof.text: Now let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$ be arbitrary and $G\in\operatorname{QCoh}(X_V)$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] and [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-fibre-dimension], $f_V$ satisfies the same family and dimension hypotheses. Repeat steps 1--3 for $f_V$ and $G$ to get $R^qf_{V,*}G=0$ for $q>1$. The affine-base formula [lem-sfb-space-affine-base-higher-image-sections] gives $H^q(X_V,G)\cong\Gamma(V,R^qf_{V,*}G)=0$. This repeats the argument for the supplied $G$ and does not require it to descend from $X$.

source.place: Tag 08EX; arbitrary-base preservation of the family hypotheses.
